children: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins on Saturday said that a "steady, gradual path seems appropriate" of modest interest rate hikes is the best way forward for monetary policy and the economy.

Speaking Saturday morning at a conference in Boston, Collins added, "The price data we’ve seen over the past three months, and the labor market on a stronger footing, does make me think that the path of policy, of rates, over the next year might be a bit higher than I had thought a couple of months ago."
With the October Consumer Price Index coming in a bit
than consensus, she's keeping an eye out on inflation potentially broadening.

She also expressed concern that there are more risks to the economy. As a result, "it's possible that the rise in medium- to longer-term rates that we've seen since the beginning of the year may actually weigh on demand more than I'm thinking,"
Collins noted those risks are two-sided, as high inflation remains a concern and a stable job market could take off. And while hiring has picked up, she said it is on the slower side.

title: Fed's Collins says 'gradual path' of rate hikes is best for the economy
